Our story

From Digital Kiribati to Empower Kiribati.

We began as Digital Kiribati with a focused conviction: when people can access digital skills, trusted information, and online services, they unlock opportunity — for learning, livelihoods, and connection across our islands.

Listening closely to communities in South Tarawa and across the outer islands quickly made one thing clear: digital inclusion matters, but it is only one part of what shapes people’s lives. Limited employment pathways for women and youth, uneven access to education and training, and the daily pressures families carry all influence what is possible.

These realities are intensified by a defining challenge of our time: climate change is an escalating threat to Kiribati’s land, livelihoods, and way of life. In a nation of low-lying atolls, resilience is not optional — it is essential.

That is why Empower Kiribati emerged: an evolution from a digital-first initiative into a community-led movement focused on opportunity, resilience, and dignity — shaped by I-Kiribati priorities, culture, and lived experience. We exist to help turn local leadership into lasting outcomes, and to connect partners around practical, deliverable solutions.

We work with NGOs, government, and regional and international organizations — bridging local knowledge with practical delivery in ways that are culturally grounded and contextually relevant.

Our mission

What we set out to do.

To empower communities in Kiribati through practical programs, partnerships, and advocacy that strengthen livelihoods, expand education and skills pathways, and build long-term resilience in the face of climate and economic change.

Our vision

Where we're heading.

A Kiribati where every person has the opportunity, tools, and support to reach their potential, contribute meaningfully, and live with dignity — even as climate pressures intensify.

Our approach

How we're different.

Empower Kiribati is locally rooted and guided by lived experience. We combine cultural understanding, community trust, and practical delivery—so solutions are designed with people, not for them. We listen first, co‑design with communities, and strengthen local partners to lead the work.

Just as importantly, we are outcomes‑driven over the long term. We don’t measure success only by what gets delivered today, but by what continues to work months and years later—when ownership is local, capability is strengthened, and progress can be maintained and improved.

In practice, that looks like:

01

Locally led

shaped by I‑Kiribati culture, language, and outer‑island realities.

02

Listen first; co‑design always

we invest in trust‑building and shared ownership from the outset.

03

Practical and evidence‑based

we prioritize approaches that are proven, measurable, and workable across dispersed atolls.

04

Inclusive by design

we center people facing the greatest barriers, including women, youth, and outer‑island communities.

05

Accountable and transparent

we communicate clearly, track progress, and learn openly.

06

Built to endure

we strengthen local partners and systems so benefits continue long after a project ends.

07

Safety‑first

we uphold strong safeguarding and a do‑no‑harm approach in everything we do.
